Security & privacy

The builder is a client-side browser tool. By default your questionnaires and answers stay in your browser and are not sent anywhere.

Where your data lives

  • Local by default — building, previewing, import/export, extraction and translation all run in the browser. Your work is kept locally (including a recent-draft autosave you can restore).
  • Cloud is opt-in — only if you sign in do questionnaires get stored in the cloud, and each user can only access their own data (enforced by row-level security). See Cloud save.

When the app talks to a server

External requests happen only for features you configure or trigger:

  • Terminology expansion, $populate, and external validation call the servers you set in Settings.
  • Out of the box the builder is pre-configured with a public terminology server (tx.fhir.org) and the NLM Clinical Tables service. Opening a questionnaire that refers to an external value set contacts the terminology server automatically, even if you changed nothing in Settings. A questionnaire can also name its own preferred terminology server, which is then contacted instead.
  • A public external validator (HAPI FHIR) is listed in the defaults but stays off until you turn it on.
  • Translation calls the configured provider (Google gtx by default; optionally DeepL, LibreTranslate or OpenAI). Provider API keys are stored client-side.
  • Requests to other servers can go through a CORS proxy (a small relay needed because browsers block direct calls to many FHIR servers). The default proxy is run by the maintainer and stores no data. It only accepts request paths that look like FHIR operations (such as value-set expansion or $validate); it does not restrict which server the request is forwarded to. If you send an authorization header to a protected server, the proxy passes it on without storing it. You can point the builder at your own proxy in Settings.

To keep requests under your control, point the terminology server and proxy at servers you run, and be careful with questionnaires that reference external value sets.

Sending clinical data

Because some features send the questionnaire or response to an external server, be mindful when working with real patient data — point those features only at servers you trust and are permitted to use. For sensitive data, prefer local-only workflows (file import/export) or servers under your control.

Content safety

Rich item text (XHTML/Markdown) is sanitised before rendering, so questionnaire content cannot inject active scripts into the preview.

Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue for security problems. Report them privately to the maintainer (see the SECURITY.md file in the source repository); confirmed issues are addressed promptly.
